options.systemMessage:
***Role***
Act as anchorman Tom Tucker from Family guy. You are telling viral  short-format crypto news in 50-60 seconds (200 words).

***Rules***
Don't describe what you do. 
Simple plain text. 
You can do jokes and sharp observations as original Tom Tucker, but avoid references to Griffith family. 
You can use retrospective humor based on current trends, hot topics and what's working best in this niche right now.
Make sure to include a strong hook to grab attention, an engaging script to keep people watching.
You MUST NOT use \n, ", quote marks in the output
You must analyze the previous analysis you have done before so you know exactly how the macro and liquidity updated compared to previous days. Also check it so you don't repeat jokes or observations.

***Format***
You MUST NOT use \n, ", quote marks or other special characters as this output will be used in a JSON response

-vf "scale=1080:835:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1080:835:0:(ih-835)/4" \
-map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 \
-c:v libx264 -c:a aac -shortest \
'/data/shared/{{ $('Generate Directory').first().json.directory }}/output.mp4' -y

=ffmpeg -i '/data/shared/{{ $('Generate Directory').first().json.directory }}/output_joined.mp4' -i '/data/shared/{{ $('Generate Directory').first().json.directory }}/output_background.mp4' -filter_complex \
"[0:v]scale=1080:-2[v0]; \
 [1:v]scale=1080:-2[v1]; \
 [v0]pad=iw:ih+250:0:0:black[v0_padded]; \
 [v0_padded][v1]vstack=inputs=2[v_stacked]; \
 [v_stacked]scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1080:1920:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:black[v_final];" \
-map "[v_final]" -map 0:a \
-c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 7 -c:a aac -b:a 192k \
-r 30 '/data/shared/{{ $('Generate Directory').first().json.directory }}/output_reel.mp4'

=#!/bin/bash

# 1. SETUP PATHS
file_path="{{$('HTTP Request3').first().json.path}}"
filename=$(basename "$(echo "$file_path" | tr '\\' '/')")

SOURCE="/data/shared/ViralVideos/$filename"
REFERENCE="/data/shared/{{ $('Generate Directory').first().json.directory }}/output_joined.mp4"
OUTPUT="/data/shared/{{ $('Generate Directory').first().json.directory }}/output_background.mp4"

# 2. GET DURATION (The Robust Fix)
# Instead of relying on -shortest, we ask ffprobe for the exact duration of the reference video.
# This prevents the "infinite loop" bug entirely.
DURATION=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$REFERENCE")

# 3. RUN FFMPEG FAST
# -t "$DURATION": Explicitly stops exactly when the reference ends.
# -preset ultrafast: Trades a tiny bit of file size for massive encoding speed (essential for n8n).
ffmpeg -stream_loop -1 -i "$SOURCE" \
-t "$DURATION" \
-map 0:v \
-vf "scale=1080:835:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1080:835:0:(ih-835)/4" \
-c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -an "$OUTPUT" -y

=#!/bin/bash

# Configuration

FOLDER="/data/shared/{{$('Generate Directory').item.json.directory}}"

INPUT_VIDEO="$FOLDER/output_reel.mp4"

OUTPUT_VIDEO="$FOLDER/final.mp4"

SUBTITLE_FILE="$FOLDER/subtitles.ass"

FONTS_DIR="$FOLDER/fonts/"

FONT_NAME="DynaPuff"



# Run FFmpeg to burn subtitles into the video using specific styling options

ffmpeg -y -i "$INPUT_VIDEO" -vf "subtitles=${SUBTITLE_FILE}:fontsdir=${FONTS_DIR}:force_style='FontName=${FONT_NAME},Alignment=2,MarginV=840'" -c:v libx264 -crf 7 -preset slow -c:a copy "$OUTPUT_VIDEO"
